Every prediction met. One function appeared and nothing else moved.

════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
WHAT ACCEPTING ACTUALLY DOES

  1. CLOSES the referring counsellor's caseload link
     (is_active = false, ended_at = now())
  2. OPENS a new link for the receiving counsellor, carrying the client's
     IDENTITY ONLY — name, contact, organisation, member id.

counsellor_clients is never repointed, because there is no mutable
counsellor_id to repoint. Karabo's old row and everything hanging off it stay
Karabo's BECAUSE THEY ARE STILL THE SAME ROWS. Nothing had to remember not to
update them.

WHAT ACCEPTING DOES NOT DO — the half that matters

  Nicola does not gain access to Karabo's notes.
  Nicola does not gain access to Karabo's bookings for that client.
  Nicola cannot even see Karabo's now-closed caseload row.
  Not before accepting, not after, not ever.

  Existing bookings keep pointing at Karabo's link and at Karabo, so they stay
  unreadable to Nicola. That is the behaviour, not an oversight to fix later.

  The only thing that crosses is the handover note Karabo WROTE ON PURPOSE for
  this referral.

WHO MAY ACCEPT

  Only the counsellor the referral was sent to. Not the referrer — she cannot
  accept on the receiver's behalf. Not Lone or Michelle — a psychosocial admin
  sees THAT a referral happened and cannot accept one, because taking on a case
  is a clinical decision, not an administrative one.

  The migration asserts this structurally: it refuses to apply if
  referral_accept mentions is_admin or is_psychosocial_admin at all.

════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
LOCAL SUITE — 51 assertions, 0 failed

The ten new ones (40-49), with the negative ones doing the real work:

  40 the REFERRING counsellor cannot accept her own referral
  41 a psychosocial admin cannot accept on anyone's behalf
  42 the receiving counsellor accepts and gets a new link
  43 accepting twice is not an error and opens no second link
  44 after accepting, Nicola STILL cannot read Karabo's note      <-- the point
  45 nor Karabo's booking for the same client                     <-- the point
  46 nor Karabo's now-closed caseload row                         <-- the point
  47 Karabo still reads her own note and booking after handing over
  48 and her caseload row is CLOSED, not deleted and not repointed
  49 Lone sees the referral was ACCEPTED, with a date and no note

Full regression, all exit 0: phase0 all, m1 22, m5 45, m5a 29, support 28,
m4 66, m4a 23, m3 51.

════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
NOTHING IS WAITING ON IT

There are zero referrals on live. This was applied so the capability exists
when Karabo and Nicola need it, not because anything was blocked.

════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
NOT BUILT, AND FLAGGED RATHER THAN ASSUMED

  THERE IS NO DECLINE PATH. A referral the receiver does not want sits
  unaccepted forever, and the referring counsellor has no signal that it was
  refused rather than not yet read. That is a real gap in the workflow, it was
  not in the brief, and it needs a decision about what a decline tells the
  referrer before it is built.

SUPERSEDED — RISK ESCALATION HAPPENS OUTSIDE THE PLATFORM

  Decided 28 Aug 2026 and permanent, for confidentiality reasons. A counsellor
  escalates by REFERRING THE CLIENT TO EXTERNAL PARTIES according to the level
  of risk. That happens out of band, the way out-of-band contact always has.

  There is NO internal flag, NO notification, and NO admin action tied to a
  risk event. The content-free nameless action for Lone described in earlier
  specs is NOT BEING BUILT — not deferred, not owed, not pending.

  This matters for anything reading `actions`: there is no risk-flag row type
  coming, so nothing should be shaped to leave room for one.

  Recorded in claude/ops-data-model-and-impact.md §2.3a and §5 item 2, and in
  claude/ops-migration-governance.md's M3b section.
